# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `bun run docs` from src/commands. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every command accepts `--json`, `-p <slug>` and `--help`.

## devit init

```
Set up Devit in the current repo and register it

Usage: devit init [dir] [options]

Creates .devit/project.yaml (commit it) and registers the project on this machine.
Slug, repo and base branch are detected from git; override them with the flags.
Running it again in an initialized repo re-registers it and changes nothing else.

Options:
      --slug <slug>        project slug (default: from the folder name)
      --name <name>        display name (default: the folder name)
      --base <branch>      branch PRs target (default: develop if it exists, else the default branch)
      --repo <owner/name>  GitHub repo (default: from the origin remote)

Global options:
  -p, --project <slug>  project to act on (default: the .devit/ above the current directory)
      --json            print JSON instead of text
  -h, --help            show help
```

## devit task add

```
Create a task

Usage: devit task add <title> [options]

Example:
  devit task add "Fix crash on login" --persona dev --status todo --priority high

Options:
  -b, --body <text>       description (markdown)
      --persona <name>    persona responsible for it
  -s, --status <status>   initial column: backlog, todo, doing, review, done (default: backlog)
      --priority <level>  low, normal or high (default: normal)
      --source <text>     where it came from, e.g. a routine name (default: user)

Global options:
  -p, --project <slug>  project to act on (default: the .devit/ above the current directory)
      --json            print JSON instead of text
  -h, --help            show help
```

## devit persona add

```
Create a persona file from a template

Usage: devit persona add <name> [options]

Writes ~/.devit/personas/<name>.md (or .devit/personas/ in the project with --local).
Edit the file to set its tools, model and instructions; see docs/personas.md.

--from copies a ready-made persona (see `devit persona examples`); --role, --model and --lead
override its settings.

Examples:
  devit persona add dev --role "Developer" --model opus
  devit persona add dev --from dev
  devit persona add boss --from lead

Options:
      --role <text>          one-line role, e.g. "Developer"
      --model <model>        model alias or id (default: sonnet)
      --lead                 make it the lead persona, which answers `devit ask`
  -i, --instructions <text>  the persona's instructions (default: a placeholder)
      --from <example>       start from an example: lead, dev, pm, writer, reviewer
      --local                the current project's .devit/personas/ instead of the global folder

Global options:
  -p, --project <slug>  project to act on (default: the .devit/ above the current directory)
      --json            print JSON instead of text
  -h, --help            show help
```

## devit playbook add

```
Create a playbook from a template or an example

Usage: devit playbook add <name> [options]

Writes .devit/playbooks/<name>.md in the current project (commit it), or ~/.devit/playbooks/ with
--global. Then edit it, and use it with `devit run <persona> --playbook <name>` or a routine.

Examples:
  devit playbook add weekly-report --from weekly-report
  devit playbook add release-notes

Options:
      --from <example>  start from an example (see `devit playbook examples`)
      --global          for every project, in ~/.devit/playbooks/

Global options:
  -p, --project <slug>  project to act on (default: the .devit/ above the current directory)
      --json            print JSON instead of text
  -h, --help            show help
```

## devit run

```
Run a persona once, on a task, a playbook or a prompt

Usage: devit run <persona> [options]

Starts the persona's agent (Claude Code, headless) in the project folder and waits for it.
The task, if any, moves to doing, then to review when the run ends (back where it was if it fails).

Examples:
  devit run dev --task 12
  devit run pm --playbook weekly-report
  devit run writer --prompt "Draft three post ideas from last week's search queries"
  devit run dev --task 12 --dry-run      # print the prompt and command, run nothing

Options:
  -t, --task <id>        task to work on
      --playbook <name>  playbook to follow (.devit/playbooks/<name>.md, then ~/.devit/playbooks/)
      --prompt <text>    what to do, or extra instructions with --task/--playbook
      --dry-run          print the prompt and the agent command instead of running
  -q, --quiet            don't stream the agent's progress

Global options:
  -p, --project <slug>  project to act on (default: the .devit/ above the current directory)
      --json            print JSON instead of text
  -h, --help            show help
```

## devit ask

```
Talk to the lead persona: ask, plan or delegate work

Usage: devit ask <message> [options]

Runs the lead persona on your message, in the current project (or across projects outside one),
and prints its answer. The lead can read the board and memory and create tasks for the others.
--continue picks up the last conversation in this project.

Examples:
  devit ask "What is in review and what is blocked?"
  devit ask "Plan the checkout redesign and split it into tasks for dev and writer"
  devit ask --continue "Make the second task high priority"

Options:
  -c, --continue        continue the last conversation with the lead here
      --persona <name>  talk to another persona instead of the lead
  -q, --quiet           print only the answer

Global options:
  -p, --project <slug>  project to act on (default: the .devit/ above the current directory)
      --json            print JSON instead of text
  -h, --help            show help
```

## devit routine add

```
Schedule a persona to run a playbook or prompt on a cron

Usage: devit routine add <name> [options]

Routines run while `devit serve` is up. A run missed while it was down runs once when it starts.
The schedule is cron in this machine's local time (set TZ to change it):
minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week, or @hourly, @daily, @weekly, @monthly.

Examples:
  devit routine add weekly-report --persona pm --cron "0 9 * * 1" --playbook weekly-report
  devit routine add sentry-triage --persona dev --cron "0 8 * * 1-5" --playbook sentry
  devit routine add friday-summary --persona pm --cron "0 17 * * fri" --global --prompt "Summarize the week across projects"

Options:
      --persona <name>   who runs it (required)
      --cron <expr>      when, e.g. "0 9 * * 1" (required)
      --playbook <name>  playbook to follow
      --prompt <text>    what to do, or extra instructions with --playbook
      --global           not tied to the current project

Global options:
  -p, --project <slug>  project to act on (default: the .devit/ above the current directory)
      --json            print JSON instead of text
  -h, --help            show help
```

## devit serve

```
Run the daemon and the web board: routines, autopickup, GitHub sync

Usage: devit serve [options]

Keeps running until stopped (Ctrl-C or SIGTERM, which interrupts running agents cleanly).
Every --interval seconds it starts:
  - routines whose time came; one missed while the daemon was down runs once on start
  - tasks in To do assigned to a persona with `autopickup: true` (a failure sends them to the backlog)
A persona runs one thing at a time. Only one daemon runs per DEVIT_HOME.

The board is at http://127.0.0.1:7420. To reach it from elsewhere, put it behind a tunnel
(Cloudflare Tunnel + Access, Tailscale, ssh -L) and allow that hostname with --allowed-host, or
serve it with --host 0.0.0.0 --token <secret>. See docs/board.md.

Every --sync-minutes it runs `devit github sync` for projects with a repo, if `gh` is logged in.
--once does a single pass and waits for its runs, without the board, for system cron or CI.

Options:
      --once                 one pass: start what is due, wait for it, exit
      --interval <seconds>   how often to look for work (default 30)
      --max-parallel <n>     runs at the same time (default 3)
      --port <port>          board port (default 7420, or DEVIT_PORT)
      --host <host>          board address (default 127.0.0.1)
      --token <secret>       require this token on the board (or DEVIT_TOKEN)
      --allowed-host <name>  hostname a tunnel serves the board on (repeatable)
      --no-web               no board, just the daemon
      --sync-minutes <n>     GitHub sync interval (default 15; 0 turns it off)

Global options:
  -p, --project <slug>  project to act on (default: the .devit/ above the current directory)
      --json            print JSON instead of text
  -h, --help            show help
```

## devit github sync

```
Import labeled GitHub issues and close tasks whose PR merged

Usage: devit github sync [options]

Uses the GitHub CLI (`gh`), logged in with `gh auth login`. For the project's repo:
  - open issues labeled `devit` (or `issue_label` in .devit/project.yaml) become backlog tasks
  - a task whose PR was merged, or whose issue was closed, moves to done
Devit only reads from GitHub. `devit serve` runs this every 15 minutes.

Options:
  -a, --all  every project with a repo

Global options:
  -p, --project <slug>  project to act on (default: the .devit/ above the current directory)
      --json            print JSON instead of text
  -h, --help            show help
```

## devit skill install

```
Install the devit skill so Claude Code and Codex can drive Devit

Usage: devit skill install [options]

Writes SKILL.md to ~/.claude/skills/devit/ (and ~/.codex/skills/devit/, ~/.agents/skills/devit/ when
those agents are installed). Run it again after upgrading Devit to update the skill. With --repo,
it goes into the current project instead (.claude/skills/devit/…), to commit with the code.

Then, in a Claude Code or Codex session, ask things like "add a task for dev to fix the login bug",
"what did the team do this week?" or "ask the lead to plan the pricing page".

Options:
      --for <agent>  claude, codex, agents or all (default: claude + the ones installed)
      --repo         in the current project's repo (.claude/skills/…) instead of your home folder

Global options:
  -p, --project <slug>  project to act on (default: the .devit/ above the current directory)
      --json            print JSON instead of text
  -h, --help            show help
```

## devit memory add

```

Example:
  devit memory add release-process --description "How releases ship" --body "PR develop → main, merge commit"
```
